**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The transition/data-return protections this rule looks for are present and sit at or above the fallback:

- **Data return/deletion (Section 11.6, survives per Section 12.4)** — reciprocal, and triggered only *at our request*, so RevMed must destroy all copies of our Confidential Information it has no surviving right to keep and **certify destruction in writing**. No walk-away risk of unilateral or immediate deletion of our data.
- **Transition assistance (Sections 12.3(c)(iv)–(vi))** — extensive, but runs *from us to RevMed* because we are the licensee and the Products revert to RevMed on termination. That is the reversion bargain, not a gap, and I did not flag or expand obligations that bind us.
- **Our upside on exit** — Section 12.3(b) (perpetual, royalty-free licenses on expiry), 12.3(c)(iii)/(d)(ii) (sell-off period), and 12.3(e) (RevMed must give us data copies and "all reasonable assistance" in the change-of-control scenario where we keep the program).

Noted in the rationale but not redlined (minor sub-elements short of preferred): Section 11.6 provides destruction only, with no machine-readable return option and "promptly" rather than a fixed 30-day outside date; and Section 12.3(d)(i) grants us a license on termination for RevMed's breach/insolvency without accompanying know-how/data delivery (partly mitigated by the Section 7.2 manufacturing know-how transfer).
